data.narrative:
The Nuclear Company is a Series A frontier-tech venture in the nuclear energy sector. The valuation universe comprises 11 peers: 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private-stage firms including Fuse Energy, X-Energy, Oklo, and Nano Nuclear Energy. The company has raised $50M+ to date.

Stage-progression methodology is the applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised ($50M) as a proxy baseline and applying a typical Series A-to-next-stage multiplier of 2.0x yields an implied valuation of $100M. The peer-median method was not applied due to insufficient narrow comparables—while four same-sector peers exist, filtering for identical stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier produced fewer than three datapoints. A broader sectoral median would introduce unacceptable noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $85M (low) to $115M (high), with a median of $100M. This range reflects reliance on a single methodology and carries material uncertainty around stage-progression calibration in early-stage deeptech. Key unknowns include the company's capital efficiency relative to peers, progress toward commercial milestones, and regulatory pathway clarity—factors not quantifiable from available comps data. Additional valuation conviction would require either expanded peer-set depth or internal metrics on cash burn, time-to-revenue, and technical de-risking progress.
